'''Kathrin Bringmann''' (born 8 May 1977) is a German [[number theorist]] in the [[University of Cologne]], [[Germany]], who has made fundamental contributions to the theory of [[mock theta function]]s.

==Education and career==

Kathrin Bringmann was born on 8 May 1977, in Muenster, Germany. She passed the State Examinations in Mathematics and Theology at the [[University of Würzburg]], Germany, in 2002, and obtained a Diploma in Mathematics at Würzburg in 2003. She received PhD in 2004 from [[University of Heidelberg]] under the supervision of {{ill|Winfried Kohnen|de}}.

During 2004–07, she was Edward Burr Van Vleck Assistant Professor with the [[University of Wisconsin]] where she began her collaboration with [[Ken Ono]]. After briefly serving as an assistant professor at the [[University of Minnesota]], she joined the [[University of Cologne]], Germany, as Professor.

==Recognition==
Bringmann has been awarded the Alfried Krupp-Förderpreis for Young Professors, a one-million-Euro prize instituted by the [[Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach Foundation]]. She is the third mathematician to win this prize.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bringmann Receives One Million Euro Krupp Prize |url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=34|date=July 2, 2009|access-date=11 July 2023|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref> She has also been awarded the [[SASTRA Ramanujan Prize]] in 2009 for her contributions to "areas of mathematics influenced by the genius [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]]."<ref>[http://www.sastra.edu/mnews/2009/sep/Ramanujan_Award.htm German Professor bags SASTRA Ramanujan Award for 2009] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091004105145/http://www.sastra.edu/mnews/2009/sep/Ramanujan_Award.htm |date=4 October 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bringmann to Receive 2009 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize |url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=17|date=September 29, 2009|access-date=7 July 2023|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref>

She was the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2015.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv/preise-auszeichnungen|title=Preise und Auszeichnungen|publisher=[[German Mathematical Society]]|language=German|access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>

A book by Bringmann with [[Amanda Folsom]], [[Ken Ono]], and Larry Rolen, ''Harmonic Maass Forms and Mock Modular Forms: Theory and Applications'' (Amer. Math. Soc., 2018),<ref name="Bringmann Folsom Ono Rolen 2017 p. ">{{cite book | last=Bringmann | first=Kathrin | last2=Folsom | first2=Amanda | last3=Ono | first3=Ken | last4=Rolen | first4=Larry | title=Harmonic Maass forms and mock modular forms : theory and applications | publication-place=Providence, Rhode Island | date=2017 | isbn=978-1-4704-1944-8 | oclc=989726785 | page=}}</ref> won the 2018 [[PROSE Awards|Prose Award]] for Best Scholarly Book in Mathematics from the [[Association of American Publishers]].<ref name="Schwartz">{{cite web | last=Schwartz | first=Larry | title=Association of American Publishers | website=Minnesota State University Moorhead | url=https://web.mnstate.edu/schwartz/assocampub.html | access-date=2023-02-10}}</ref>
